chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abi Jamiilah, from Jabir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said:

I once gave a dinar in charity. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me: 'Do you not know, O Ali, that the charity of a believer does not leave his hand until seventy devils are released from it, all of them commanding him not to do so. And it does not fall into the hand of the beggar until it falls into the hand of the Lord, exalted is His majesty.'
Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities, and that it is Allah who is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful?
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of charity (Sadaqah) in Shia tradition regarding the release of devils?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual struggle of charity, where seventy devils attempt to deter the giver before the wealth departs his possession. The text emphasizes that the charity remains under divine guardianship until it reaches the recipient, reinforcing the concept of Allah's direct acceptance of charitable acts. This is supported by the recitation of Surah At-Tawbah 9:104, linking the act of giving with divine forgiveness and mercy.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 12.  Imam  Muhammad  Baqir  (a.s.)  narrates  that  Amirul Momineen (a.s.) said that once he gave a dinar as Sadaqah.

The  Holy  Prophet  (s.a.w.s.)  told  him,  “O  Ali!  Don’t  you know, that before a believer gives Sadaqah seventy Satans are released and they plead him not to do so. This Sadaqah passes through the hands of Allah before reaching the hands of the beggar.”
Then he recited the verse: ‘Don’t you know that only Allah accepts the repentance of the servants and takes  Sadaqah.  Surely  Allah  is  the  Greatest  Forgiver  and Most Merciful.”
